test_title: PYST 3: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:17 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

In her heart, Sheila knew that her paths with Rahul would _________ soon.
solution:
The correct answer is '**cross**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**paths cross**" is a common idiomatic expression in English that means to meet or come across someone, often by chance.
 
• Option 1, "**change**," doesn't fit grammatically in the context of this sentence. Paths themselves don't change; people might change their paths, but the paths aren't the agents of change.
 
• Option 2, "**end**," doesn't work in this context because paths don't typically end with someone else, unless the sentence was rephrased to imply two people walking on the same path together.
 
• Option 3, "**merge**," can imply that Sheila and Rahul would join together in some way, potentially on a more permanent basis than simply meeting. This might be suitable in a different context, but generally "paths cross" is more idiomatic.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: "**In her heart, Sheila knew that her paths with Rahul would cross soon.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• Idiomatic expressions or phrases can be different across different cultures and languages. It's essential to understand the commonly used phrases and their implied meanings in English to capture nuances in many contexts. "Paths cross" is such an idiom that's commonly used to denote meeting someone at an intersection of paths (both literally and figuratively).
